DECISION1_OPTS.t: A. Trust it, since the JSON parses without error
DECISION1_OPTS.why: Parsing without error only tells you the SYNTAX was fine. It says nothing about the 8% missing an optional field or the 1% with a value outside your allowed set, both of which parse cleanly and still break the downstream API.

DECISION1_OPTS.t: B. Retry every response automatically, just in case
DECISION1_OPTS.why: Retrying everything wastes a model call and money on the 91% of responses that were already fine, and it doesn't even fix the problem: a retried call can produce the exact same missing field or bad enum value again, nothing about a retry guarantees a different outcome.

DECISION1_OPTS.t: C. Validate the schema, and explicitly handle the missing-field and invalid-value cases before the API call
DECISION1_OPTS.why: This is the only option that acts on what you actually know: two specific, named failure modes with measured rates. A schema validator that checks required-vs-optional correctly and checks enum membership catches both before they ever reach the downstream API, which is exactly the kind of check a service boundary needs.

DECISION1_OPTS.t: D. Ask the model to "be more careful" in the prompt
DECISION1_OPTS.why: A stronger instruction can lower the RATE (this module's few-shot lesson), it can't lower it to zero, and it does nothing for the two specific failure modes you've already measured. You have real data on how this model behaves; engineer around the data, don't just ask nicer.
